Data.title: Polymarket Makes a Remarkable Move for Bitcoin (BTC), Ethereum (ETH), Solana (SOL), and XRP! Time Limit Reduced to 5 Minutes!
Data.body: While attention in Bitcoin and altcoins is focused on the FED decision today, Polymarket has released news regarding BTC, Ethereum, Solana, and XRP. Polymarket US announced that it will launch five-minute price direction prediction contracts for Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana, and XRP on October 27, 2026. According to the announcement, the new product allows users in the US to take positions on whether the four crypto assets will rise or fall in the short term. The contracts are based on whether the underlying crypto asset will remain above or below its starting level at the end of a five-minute timeframe. Instead of directly purchasing the underlying crypto asset, users buy contracts for the expected outcome. The contracts offer two possible outcomes: a rise or a fall. Winning positions are paid at $1 per contract, while losing positions are terminated without payment. How Are Prices Determined? According to the explanation, instead of using a single instantaneous price, the results are calculated by averaging the index observations taken in the last 60 seconds before closing. Accordingly, the CF Benchmarks Bitcoin Real-Time Index is used for Bitcoin; and the relevant dollar-based real-time indices are used for Ethereum, Solana, and XRP. A closing price equal to the starting price is also considered an “up” result. In this context, the method aims to reduce the impact of sudden price movements at the end of the term on the outcome. However, short time intervals, market volatility, and transaction costs pose significant risks for users. Polymarket US had previously launched 15-minute cryptocurrency prediction markets. The introduction of five-minute contracts covering four assets expands the platform’s short-term prediction options. The US platform is operated by QCX LLC, separately from the international Polymarket service, and operates as a market overseen by the US Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC). *This is not investment advice. Data.title: Galaxy Digital: Its Biggest Growth Opportunity Is Still Waiting For A Tenant
Data.body: Summary Galaxy Digital maintains a Buy rating despite a 26% stock decline, driven by Helios data center growth and long-term revenue visibility. Helios Phase I is operational, Phase II adds 260 MW by 2027, and all three phases are leased to CoreWeave, targeting over $1 billion annual rental income. Helios II’s 830 MW approved capacity is a key growth catalyst; securing a creditworthy tenant and favorable financing terms is crucial for future earnings. GLXY’s financing risk persists, with high leverage and dependence on CoreWeave’s creditworthiness, but the lower valuation and rising 2028 earnings forecasts support the Buy thesis. In August I wrote about Galaxy Digital ( GLXY ) and gave it a Buy rating at a stock price of around $23. The buy case was about Helios; this is where it builds data centers for AI. I believed that 2031 is a much better year to look at than this year. The stock price is now around $17.10, which means that it has declined about 26% in almost 2 months. Galaxy reported third quarter earnings and posted an enormous net profit of $323 million, compared to a loss of $85 million in Q2. Adjusted EBITDA even rose from minus $77 million to $455 million. That is a really impressive recovery. However, out of that $455 million, $395 million came from Treasury & Corporate, which was mostly due to appreciation in investment values. The two operational divisions together accounted for only $60 million in adjusted EBITDA. Of that, $69 million came from Data Centers, while Digital Assets still posted a $9 million loss. Helios is starting to work, while the other division is not yet structurally profitable. The data center division even operated almost at break-even in terms of net profit. Against $69 million in adjusted EBITDA, there were $75 million in interest expenses and $17 million in depreciation, so there was no profit left at the bottom line. Helios Is Now Really Starting To Contribute Helios Campus Update (Galaxy Digital Q3 2026 Presentation) Back in August, I found the completion of Phase I important because it will show us that it can build such a large project. Now it succeeded. The 133 MW of IT capacity generated about $79 million in rental revenue in the past quarter. The data center division achieved $69 million in adjusted EBITDA, compared to $11 million in Q2. The next step is bigger because Phase II adds 260 MW of IT capacity (almost double), and the first data halls will be completed starting in Q2 2027. After completion, about $675 million in annual base rent is expected. Together with Phase I, Galaxy is expected to reach an annualized rental revenue of $800 to $850 million by the end of 2027. Phase III will deliver another 133 MW in 2028. The three phases have been leased to CoreWeave for 15 years and are expected to generate over $1 billion in annual rental income. Those revenues are predictable as long as CoreWeave pays. However, there is a small catch considering its profitability because Phase II requires about $4 billion in construction costs. Its financing consists of $3.5 billion in bonds at an interest rate of 9.875%. So that amounts to a hefty $346 million in annual interest. Why I Find Helios II More Interesting The Helios Data Center Campus (Galaxy Digital Q3 2026 Presentation) My growth catalyst is still the 830 MW of approved capacity at Helios II. That is additional capacity on top of the 800 MW already leased to CoreWeave. Galaxy now has a total pipeline of 5.73 GW, but I attach less value to that for now because much still lacks definitive power allocations and tenants. For example, things went less well at Caspian. Galaxy had hoped for a fixed allocation of power capacity, but ERCOT wants to investigate the project further first. So it remains uncertain how much capacity Galaxy will ultimately receive. We will get more clarity on this in April 2027. The situation is different at Helios II because that capacity has already been approved, whereas developers elsewhere are running into delays and regulations. I think this could improve Galaxy's negotiating position. In the summer, talks about a lease were already well advanced, but Galaxy ultimately declined the proposed terms. I think that is a good decision. These are long-term contracts, and accepting unfavorable terms could cost Galaxy hundreds of millions in potential earnings over the coming years. But waiting also comes at a price. Helios II could provide capacity in 2028, and about $230 million has already been committed for electrical installations and equipment with long lead times. Without a tenant, it is unclear for me what return those investments will yield. In August, I calculated that leasing half of that 830 MW (on terms comparable to those at CoreWeave) could generate about $620 million in additional annual revenue. That is still an estimate because the actual rental price, construction costs, and financing are unknown. However, if Galaxy can lease even part of that to a financially strong second customer, I think its earnings potential in 2031 could be much higher than I expect. A financially strong tenant could also help Galaxy secure better financing terms. For example, on $3 billion of debt, a one percentage point lower interest rate would save Galaxy $30 million annually. Digital Assets Grows But Profit Lags Global Markets (Galaxy Digital Q3 2026 Presentation) The other division also deserves attention because Galaxy's trading volumes rose by 12% while the broader market barely grew. The average loan book increased by 27% to $1.8 billion. Meanwhile, the number of trading relationships rose by only 1%. Galaxy therefore seems to be doing more business with existing customers. However, Digital Assets' adjusted gross profit rose only from $66 million to $71 million, and adjusted EBITDA remained negative. Staked assets grew by 64% to $4.6 billion, which was mainly due to higher crypto prices, although over $400 million in new capital also flowed in around the quarter. Therefore, more assets on the platform do not mean the same amount of additional fees. I find the partnership with BNY more interesting in the longer term. Galaxy is helping to build infrastructure for digital assets. If Galaxy can enter into similar partnerships with other banks, then I think this could become an interesting source of recurring revenue. Financing Remains My Biggest Concern At the end of the third quarter, the data center division had about $6.8 billion in assets and $5.3 billion in liabilities. Galaxy also holds $4.9 billion in cash, stablecoins, and US Treasury bonds. That sounds comfortable, but that amount increased largely due to the new Phase II loan. I therefore do not consider that amount as freely available profit. Moreover, another $445 million in convertible bonds matures in December. I therefore find the new authorization to repurchase another $200 million in shares remarkable. At the current stock price that might be attractive, but I believe Galaxy also needs that capital for future projects. And then there is CoreWeave. The leases run for 15 years, whereas CoreWeave's contracts with its customers last around 5 years on average. Galaxy has a contract with CoreWeave itself, so it does not have a direct payment guarantee from the one using Helios. As a result, CoreWeave's creditworthiness remains the determining factor. My View At a stock price of around $17, Galaxy is about 26% cheaper than during my previous article in August. Since August, the earnings forecast for 2028 has risen from $0.17 to $0.32 per share. With the lower stock price, the P/E for that year has fallen from about 141x to 49x now. Which is still expensive, and 2028 remains a transitional year for Helios. That is why I prefer to look at 2031. To justify the current stock price at 20x times annual earnings, about $330 million in net profit is needed by then, before any additional dilution. I believe that this is achievable. Therefore, my Buy rating remains unchanged. The CoreWeave contracts offer the visibility of substantial revenue growth, and the lower stock price allows for setbacks. I believe Helios II could make the real difference. For that, I would like to see a creditworthy tenant with financing terms so that the extra EBITDA actually generates more earnings per share. That will be my main focus in 2027.

Data.title: AI Debt Fears Are Sending Money Into US Treasuries, but America's $40 Trillion Debt Problem Remains
Data.body: Key takeaways AI financing fears push investors toward safer Treasuries US government debt approaches $40 trillion amid deficits Inflation and borrowing costs complicate the Fed outlook Wall Street's biggest bond-market concern may no longer be the Federal Reserve. Investors are increasingly watching whether the debt-funded artificial intelligence boom can survive its own enormous financing requirements. US Treasury bonds have recovered from their early-October selloff, even as inflation remains elevated and another interest rate increase remains possible in December. According to Reuters , concerns about financing problems in AI infrastructure have encouraged investors to shift money from riskier technology investments into government debt. The change is significant because the US 10-year Treasury yield has risen approximately 84 basis points during 2026 despite the recent recovery in bond prices. AI Debt Fears Are Driving Money Into Treasury Bonds The bond market's recovery began as investors questioned whether AI infrastructure companies could continue financing expensive data centers, chips and electricity contracts. Corporate borrowing tied to artificial intelligence has expanded rapidly, with Goldman Sachs estimating that hyperscaler debt issuance could reach $420 billion in 2027, approximately 60% above projected 2026 levels. But investors are becoming more selective. CoreWeave, one of Nvidia's major cloud-computing partners, recently saw its bond yields approach 15% , reflecting concerns about its borrowing requirements and ability to finance additional capacity. The company's credit-default swaps also exceeded 1,000 basis points , suggesting investors were demanding substantially greater compensation for potential credit losses. Those developments help explain the contrast between weak AI credit markets and stronger demand for US government securities. When investors purchase Treasuries, bond prices rise and yields fall. The mechanism works independently of changes to the Fed's benchmark interest rate. The $40 Trillion US Debt Problem Has Not Disappeared Despite the recent rally, Treasury investors face a separate challenge: Washington's growing borrowing requirements. US federal debt stands around $40 trillion, while annual budget deficits remain near 6% of gross domestic product. The government must regularly issue additional securities to finance spending and refinance existing obligations, increasing the supply investors must absorb. Coinpaper previously examined how Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent's bond buybacks could improve market liquidity without eliminating underlying borrowing pressure. That problem became visible when Treasury yields reached approximately 5.35% earlier in October, their highest levels since 2002. Even the recent recovery has not erased those concerns. PIMCO previously described government bonds as unusually attractive following the yield surge, highlighting how Treasury valuations could appeal to investors seeking protection from technology-market volatility. Why the Fed May No Longer Control the Entire Bond Story The Federal Reserve is widely expected to hold its benchmark rate steady at the October 28 meeting, although investors remain concerned about another increase in December. Persistent inflation and elevated energy prices could encourage policymakers to maintain restrictive borrowing conditions. Meanwhile, AI-related credit risks have created a different influence on financial markets. As Coinpaper's examination of AI financing explained, developers increasingly borrow against future computing revenue before expensive infrastructure begins generating sufficient cash. That creates a potential vulnerability when demand disappoints or refinancing costs rise. The consequences were also explored in a recent analysis of $466 billion in AI debt , including risks facing bondholders, private lenders and institutional investors.

Data.title: Adyen Stock Plunges 12% Despite Revenue Growth as Profit Margin Outlook Weakens
Data.body: Key takeaways Adyen shares plunge despite stronger-than-expected quarterly revenue growth Company cuts 2026 EBITDA margin target to 50% AI billing expansion drives spending as profitability expectations weaken Adyen shares plunged approximately 12% in Amsterdam trading on Wednesday, October 28, despite the Dutch payments company's quarterly revenue and transaction volumes beating analysts' forecasts. The selloff followed a surprise reduction in Adyen's 2026 EBITDA margin target from approximately 52% to 50%, alongside the withdrawal of its longer-term profitability objective. According to Adyen's official Q3 business update , net revenue rose 23% year over year to €738.1 million, exceeding expectations of €730.3 million. Processed payment volumes increased 30% to €451.1 billion, also beating forecasts. Adyen Stock Sinks as Profit Margin Forecast Falls Adyen's revised outlook reflects plans to accelerate investment in employees, software and recently acquired businesses. The company expects an EBITDA margin of 50% this year, compared with approximately 52% previously. It also discontinued its ambition to achieve a margin above 55% by 2028. Management said the change would provide flexibility to expand its payments, billing, loyalty and financial products. However, investors reacted negatively to losing visibility into longer-term profitability. The stock's decline extended its year-to-date losses to approximately 40%, according to Reuters. The reaction resembles earlier pressure on PayPal shares , when concerns about growth and profit margins overshadowed the company's established payments business. A similar disconnect appeared during PayPal's second-quarter recovery , when stronger forecasts helped lift shares despite persistent profitability challenges. AI Billing and Acquisitions Push Adyen's Costs Higher Adyen's investment strategy increasingly extends beyond traditional payment processing. Recent acquisitions of Talon.One and Orb expanded its capabilities in customer loyalty management and billing software, including products serving companies that charge customers for AI model usage. Co-CEO Ingo Uytdehaage told Reuters that growing demand for billing services was encouraging further hiring. Adyen expects to add approximately 1,000–1,100 employees during 2026. The company already serves major businesses including Microsoft and LVMH, while expanding partnerships with GetYourGuide, Toast and other international merchants. Its Platforms division recorded 46% revenue growth, significantly outperforming the broader business. Unified Commerce revenue increased 29%, while Digital revenue rose 16%. The expansion comes as financial technology companies compete to offer more services alongside conventional transactions. For example, Stripe's interest in PayPal earlier this year illustrated the consolidation pressures surrounding established payments providers. Meanwhile, SoFi's latest earnings demonstrated how financial services platforms are expanding revenue through broader product offerings. Why Investors Are Questioning Fintech Valuations Adyen maintained its 2026 constant-currency revenue growth forecast of 21%–23% and expects capital expenditure to remain around 7% of net revenue. However, the company will not provide new 2027 financial objectives until February, leaving investors without its previous medium-term profitability benchmark. The broader payments industry faces increasing competition from both traditional fintech providers and blockchain-based settlement infrastructure. Visa's expanding stablecoin strategy and the development of OpenUSD illustrate how established companies are exploring alternative payment networks.

Data.title: Expert: Why XRP Didn’t Pump After Ripple Received Banking Approval
Data.body: Ripple recently received final approval from the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency to establish Ripple National Trust Bank, a federally supervised national trust bank. The approval was a significant regulatory milestone. It also left a portion of the XRP community visibly frustrated because it didn’t triggers a massive a XRP price rally. X Finance Bull Addresses the Confusion Crypto commentator X Finance Bull posted a response on X to the growing questions circulating in the XRP community . His position was clear. “A banking license doesn’t mean the price has to skyrocket overnight,” he wrote. He listed adoption, liquidity, and real usage as the factors that matter long-term. He also confirmed his outlook remains strong. “I’m still extremely bullish on $XRP,” he said, adding that he expects “some big months ahead.” BOOM RIPPLE $XRP RECEIVES FINAL OCC APPROVAL FOR ITS NATIONAL TRUST BANK! RLUSD reserve management and institutional digital asset custody under federal supervision. I'm extremely bullish on $XRP ! Full breakdown coming today. Do you realize how big this is? pic.twitter.com/gRZ6hz0tLP — X Finance Bull (@Xfinancebull) October 26, 2026 Community Reactions Split on Expectations Responses to the post revealed a divide in how XRP holders are processing the news. One commenter, Fran, pushed back on the expectation of an immediate price reaction. “Did people really expect a trust bank charter to show up on the chart the next day?” she wrote . “That kind of news usually plays out over quarters, not candles.” The comment from BULLS AND BEARS took a different angle. “Well, news like this ought to have triggered a price surge,” they wrote. “It was significant, major news.” They also referenced the experience of long-term holders, noting that those who held XRP had “been in the red for years” while other assets made gains. Two Different Timelines The exchange reflects a genuine tension in the XRP community. Some holders entered years ago and have endured extended periods of underperformance relative to other digital assets. For them, a regulatory approval of this scale carries weight beyond the technical. It represents a potential turning point after a long wait. X Finance Bull’s argument is that institutional milestones do not translate into immediate price movement. The OCC approval strengthens Ripple’s regulatory foundation and enables new banking activities, including managing reserves for RLUSD and providing fiduciary digital asset custody services. Those functions take time to build out and integrate. What Comes Next for Ripple The approval marks the conclusion of a process that began with conditional OCC approval in December 2025. Ripple National Trust Bank now operates as a federally chartered institution within the regulated financial system. Whether that translates into price appreciation, and on what timeline, remains the central question for XRP holders watching the space closely. Data.title: C2FO and Ripple Bring Instant-Pay Settlement Plans to XRP Ledger
Data.body: TL;DR: C2FO and Ripple say their Instant Pay initiative will use the XRP Ledger and RLUSD to settle financing associated with approved supplier invoices. The official source also identifies specific limits or future steps, so implementation and market impact should not be assumed. C2FO and Ripple say their Instant Pay initiative will use the XRP Ledger and RLUSD to settle financing associated with approved supplier invoices. For digital-asset markets, the important issue is less the announcement in isolation than the channel through which it could affect users, capital or network activity. The latest development deserves attention, but its relevance depends on the facts published by the organisation behind it and the work still required to make it matter. What the primary announcement establishes Suppliers on conventional payment terms can wait 30, 60 or 90 days after delivery, while early-payment arrangements may still face bank-settlement delays. C2FO says its established Early Pay programs have enabled more than 520 billion in accelerated working capital; that historical figure is not Instant Pay usage. The new design keeps agreed invoice terms intact while participating capital providers fund accelerated payments and RLUSD settles the payment on XRPL. Ripple describes the XRP Ledger as operating continuously with settlement in roughly three to five seconds, and C2FO is inviting interested firms to a waitlist. Why this could matter for crypto markets Trade finance is an unusually concrete test of tokenization because the receivable already exists and the practical challenge is getting money to the supplier. The important distinction is between changing a company’s contractual payment terms and reducing the time money spends in transit after financing is approved. If capital providers and recipients are properly integrated, faster settlement could make an existing financing product more useful. For financial institutions, a technical link is only the beginning. They must also settle liability, account for funds, control access and recover from a failed transfer. That is why announced partnerships are best judged by operating detail rather than by the number of logos appearing in a release. That distinction matters to investors trying to separate a plausible structural change from a headline that may not immediately move price or onchain activity. The limits of the headline Being on a waitlist is not the same as a fully deployed service. No adoption volumes for Instant Pay, detailed fees or universal availability have been disclosed in the source announcement. Consider the difference between holding a token and using it in an everyday business process. Treasury teams and trading desks need reconciliation, internal approvals, liquidity at the point of conversion and an auditable record. Projects that solve those edges may have more practical impact than projects that simply shorten onchain confirmation times. The wider context C2FO Instant Pay on XRP Ledger sits within a wider shift toward trade finance. This area has a recurring challenge: the benefits are easiest to describe before the operational details are complete. Different stakeholders measure success differently. A user wants clarity and predictable access; an operator wants reliable controls and manageable costs; an institution wants accountability if something fails. Those perspectives can be in tension, and the source announcement should be read with that in mind. The distinction also shapes how to read future updates. A new partnership, proposal or software version is a verifiable milestone. Adoption, consistent performance and financial effects require additional evidence. That is why follow-up reporting should distinguish released features, planned features and measured use rather than combining them into one claim. What to watch next Watch for customer pilots, capital-provider commitments, fees, geography and evidence that faster ledger settlement produces quicker receipt of usable fiat funds for suppliers. Adoption is rarely a single launch moment. It typically moves from a commercial agreement to limited implementation, onboarding, real transaction volume and eventually routine usage. Keeping those stages separate matters when evaluating institutional blockchain announcements. The next evidence should come from official implementation updates and measurable outcomes, not from assuming that a news release guarantees adoption or a token-price response. Primary source: C2FO Instant Pay on XRP Ledger (published 2026-10-27). This article was written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

Data.title: China leads US in robotics funding even as Beijing warns of a bubble
Data.body: China has invested more than the United States in robotics venture funding this year, drawing $13.2 billion against America’s $12.1 billion. These hefty investments continue even as Beijing’s planners warn of an investment bubble and Washington drafts rules to keep Chinese robots out. How much did Chinese startups pour into robotics? Global venture funding reportedly reached $9.9 billion in the third quarter of 2026, more than twice the $4.3 billion recorded a year earlier. Across the first three quarters of 2026, the sector is up roughly 185% year over year. China has invested $13.2 billion so far this year, with the U.S. close behind at $12.1 billion. Germany, on the other hand, is far behind with only $1.7 billion invested. Chinese startups like Guangzhou’s Xpeng Robotics and Shenzhen’s AI² Robotics raised $900 million and $736 million Series C, respectively. In the U.S., Travis Kalanick’s Atoms and Pittsburgh’s Skild AI, which collected $1.4 billion for its Skild Brain model, drew billion-dollar checks. Of the roughly 75 robotics companies on Crunchbase’s unicorn board that raised in the past three years, 45 joined just this year. Ulrik Stig Hansen, the co-CEO of data-layer firm Encord, said that physical AI is just starting to take off. Despite China’s lead, its own government has urged caution. In late November 2025, Li Chao, a spokeswoman for the National Development and Reform Commission, told reporters in Beijing that China now has more than 150 humanoid robot makers. She warned that too many nearly identical products could crowd out spending on research. Investment in China’s physical AI companies dropped by 40.1% in one month, from 19.4 billion yuan in August to 11.6 billion yuan in September. Total investment for the third quarter was 33.3 billion yuan, which is 28.7% lower than it was in the first half of the year. Some state-linked investors have stopped looking at new physical AI deals altogether. The slowdown is due to an informal warning, known as “window guidance,” that China’s securities regulator issued in September. Humanoid robot startups that want to go public now have to show steady revenue, shrinking losses, or real innovation. The warnings intensified when shares of Unitree Robotics , China’s best-known humanoid maker, took a nosedive and fell by half from their peak after listing in Shanghai. Still AgiBot, which is ranked alongside Unitree as a sector heavyweight, is raising 1 billion to 1.5 billion yuan at a valuation near 50 billion yuan. What robotics rules are being drafted by the U.S.? As Chinese firms raise and build, Washington is trying to shut the door. On June 3, three House members, John Moolenaar, Jay Obernolte, and Jennifer McClellan, introduced the GUARD Act. It would let national security agencies check humanoid and four-legged robots made by rival countries and ban imports that are seen as a threat. On July 28, the FCC added foreign-made advanced robots to its Covered List. These robots can’t get FCC approval unless the Department of War gives conditional permission. Separately, the House passed a defense bill whose Section 163 would stop the Pentagon from buying or operating Chinese, Russian, or Iranian humanoid systems. Crypolitan reported that Chinese manufacturers already dominate global shipments, taking 86% of more than 22,000 humanoid units shipped in the first half of 2026. Data.title: Two days of Bitcoin ETF inflows leave October about $26M in the red
Data.body: Two days of buying added $286 million into US spot Bitcoin ETFs and trimmed October’s net outflows to around $26 million. The funds had bled about $774 million over last week’s Thursday and Friday. IBIT and FBTC split Tuesday’s $176 million haul The inflows were about $176 million on Tuesday, October 27, for the second straight day of net inflows. Monday’s haul was $110 million. Most of the exit from last week took place on Thursday, October 22, with $635.49 million departing. Friday’s outflows were $137.94 million. The selloff followed a $528.40 million inflow on Oct. 21, the biggest single day for the month. Including the latest buying, net inflows year to date are about $850 million. The funds traded $1.58 billion on Tuesday. BlackRock’s IBIT added $151.46 million on Oct. 27, and Fidelity’s FBTC contributed $24.54 million. FBTC’s $14.20 billion of net assets rank second, behind IBIT. All other US spot Bitcoin funds registered zero net flow that day. Since the launch of the products in January 2024, cumulative net inflows are $57.47 billion. Net assets total $103.94 billion. This is 6.40% of Bitcoin’s market cap as of Oct. 27. SoSoValue’s US spot Bitcoin ETF dashboard shows $175.99 million in net inflows and $103.94 billion in net assets for October 27. IBIT’s cumulative net inflows totaled $66.40 billion, leaving it with net assets of $65.52 billion. Grayscale’s GBTC is sitting on -$28.00 billion in cumulative net flows. The funds lost $487.07 million on October 7 and $244.13 million on October 8, earlier in the month. Fidelity’s FBTC alone saw outflows of $197.09 million on day two. Ether funds shed another $149 million in two sessions Ether was left out of the rally. US spot Ether ETFs saw about $149 million outflows on Monday and Tuesday, after recording net outflows for four straight weeks. The group had outflows of $1.32 billion in October. The month is on pace for the heaviest withdrawals since November 2025. BlackRock’s ETHA was the biggest loser, with around $93.3 million leaving the fund on October 27. Data.title: Robinhood Lost 55% of Its Crypto Revenue. Prediction Markets Became Its New Growth Engine
Data.body: Key takeaways Robinhood's cryptocurrency revenue fell despite record company earnings Prediction markets now generate more revenue than crypto Diversification reduces dependence without eliminating speculative trading risks Robinhood built much of its reputation by making stock and cryptocurrency trading accessible to ordinary investors. But in the third quarter of 2026, one of its most recognizable businesses suffered a dramatic reversal: cryptocurrency transaction revenue collapsed 55% from a year earlier. Instead of shrinking, Robinhood's total revenue reached a record $1.42 billion. The explanation lies in a business transformation that began years earlier. According to Robinhood's October 27 earnings report , prediction markets generated $173 million during the quarter, compared with just $120 million from cryptocurrency transactions. How Robinhood Turned Predictions Into a $173 Million Business Robinhood's prediction-market experiment began in March 2025, when the company launched its hub through a partnership with federally regulated exchange Kalshi. Unlike traditional stocks, event contracts allow customers to trade on defined outcomes, such as economic announcements, sporting events or future asset prices. Traders typically purchase contracts with payouts determined by whether the specified event occurs. The business expanded rapidly. Robinhood generated just $27 million from event contracts in the third quarter of 2025, followed by $101 million in the fourth quarter. By the second quarter of 2026, prediction revenue had reached $156 million, already exceeding the company's earnings from conventional stock transactions. Three months later, event contracts produced $173 million, while customers traded a record 16.4 billion contracts. However, contracts traded are not equivalent to revenue. Robinhood earns money through its transaction arrangements, meaning the number of contracts, fees and trading activity all matter. The company also operates Rothera, its exchange and clearinghouse venture with Susquehanna, adding another layer to its prediction-market expansion . Why Crypto's Collapse Didn't Stop Robinhood's Growth Crypto revenue fell from $268 million to $120 million year over year, reflecting lower participation and trading activity. Robinhood's earlier earnings had already demonstrated how quickly cryptocurrency income could weaken when market enthusiasm faded. But other businesses filled the gap. Options revenue increased 31% to $399 million, equity transactions generated $121 million, and net interest revenue contributed another $415 million. Meanwhile, Robinhood Gold subscriptions reached 5.2 million, up 34%, while total platform assets increased to $396 billion. The company is also developing blockchain infrastructure. Its Robinhood Chain generated $26 million in attributable Q3 crypto revenue, demonstrating that digital assets remain part of the strategy. Is Robinhood Really Becoming Less Dependent on Speculation? Diversification provides Robinhood with more ways to generate revenue, but it does not automatically guarantee stability. Prediction markets depend heavily on trading activity, just as cryptocurrencies and options do. Their rapid growth also introduces regulatory uncertainty, particularly around sports-related contracts. The distinction between prediction markets and sportsbooks has become especially important as states challenge certain event contracts. Robinhood's net income still declined 14% to $476 million despite record revenue, showing that business expansion carries costs.

Data.title: Securitize: The Tokenization Opportunity Is Clearer Than The Investment Case
Data.body: Summary Securitize is trying to capitalize on the real-world asset tokenization opportunity with its regulated, vertically integrated platform. There could be significant upside if tokenization accelerates, but competitive and regulatory uncertainties create multiple layers of risk. SECZ's recent financial performance has also been disappointing, adding to doubts about the strength of the business. Given the uncertainty involved, I believe that Securitize's valuation is difficult to justify, meaning the probability of poor returns going forward is high. Securitize ( SECZ ) is a financial market infrastructure company that is trying to bring real-world assets on-chain through tokenization. The company provides the technology and regulated infrastructure that enable tokenization while also owning regulated transfer-agent and fund-administration businesses. There could be significant upside if real-world assets migrate on-chain, but there is also enormous uncertainty. There are a range of potential competitors, including both legacy financial institutions and tokenization disruptors. The key question for investors is therefore not just whether assets will be tokenized, but if Securitize can establish a sustainable competitive advantage as financial infrastructure evolves. Given the uncertainty involved, I believe that Securitize's valuation is difficult to justify, meaning the probability of poor returns going forward is high. Market Tokenization is the process of turning real-world assets, including treasuries, private credit and equity funds, and real estate, into digital tokens that are generally stored on blockchains. These tokens represent ownership in the underlying asset and can provide a number of advantages, including: Faster settlement Greater transparency Fractional ownership Improved liquidity Broader access to private markets 24/7 trading Improved efficiency Not all of these benefits are guaranteed, though. For example, access depends on regulations, and liquidity is a function of supply and demand. Tokenization can be either issuer-sponsored or via a third-party. Third-party tokens are derivatives that don't provide direct ownership of the underlying asset and can be based on assets that are held in custody by the third-party or entirely synthetic. This is a somewhat contentious issue, with a number of high-profile private companies pushing back against attempts to tokenize their stock. It is also likely to become a more important distinction as regulations mature. In the case of equities, functionality that needs to be encompassed by tokenization includes issuance, distribution, trading, clearing, and settlement. It is important to recognize that the benefits of tokenization vary across these functions and that tokenization is unlikely to replace all existing infrastructure. While smart contracts could help automate issuance, cap-table management, compliance, and corporate actions, investment banks are likely to remain important. Regulated distribution and custody are also likely to remain necessary. Tokenization has the potential to reduce some post-trade processing and settlement risk, but many CCP functions (netting, margining, default management, etc.) are likely to remain necessary. Tokenization could disintermediate a number of incumbents, like DTCC, brokers, and custodians. However, a number of these companies are embracing tokenization to try and avoid disruption. In particular, it seems likely that companies involved in settlement/ownership will either partner with tokenization companies or introduce their own solutions to maintain their existing positions. Figure 1: Traditional Value Chain versus Tokenized Value Chain (source: Securitize) The value of assets expected to be tokenized is enormous, but estimates vary widely (2-30 trillion USD in 2030). Much of the volume is expected to come from US treasuries, and tokenized equities are also expected to be a growth driver. The market is currently only worth 17 billion USD at the moment, though, meaning adoption is largely speculative at this point. It should also be noted that the market opportunity for companies like Securitize is a tiny fraction of the assets tokenized. In addition, significant parts of the market, like stablecoins, likely won't be accessible to companies like Securitize. There are also opportunities like regulated DeFi lending and yield-bearing CeFi collateral. For example, using tokenized RWAs as collateral or borrowing stablecoins while retaining asset exposure. Figure 2: Projected Tokenized Asset Market by Asset Class - trillion USD (source: Securitize) The tokenized treasury market is leading RWA growth, and this is an area where Securitize has some traction. The company has also found success with CLO funds, alternative asset funds, and to a lesser extent equities. Figure 3: Traditional Market TAM and Tokenized Opportunity in 2030 (source: Securitize) Part of the reason for the embryonic state of the tokenization market is that the regulatory landscape is still forming. The CLARITY Act aims to establish a clear division of regulatory authority between the SEC and CFTC. Digital commodities would be regulated by the CFTC, while tokenized securities would be covered by the SEC. The Senate failed to advance the act in September, although this isn't that important for Securitize. Regulatory clarity from the passage of the act could help to lower the cost of launching products and encourage institutions to participate, but direct benefits would likely be modest. More importantly, the SEC has announced conditional exemptive relief in tokenized securities trading. This covers qualifying tokenized stocks that preserve the rights associated with the underlying shares, meaning it excludes synthetic exposure products. The exemption provides conditional relief from exchange registration for qualifying tokenized securities venues and from dealer registration for certain liquidity providers. While there was no blanket prohibition on tokenized stocks, existing securities laws were designed around conventional exchanges. The SEC has also proposed modernizing transfer-agent rules in support of blockchain-based securities issuance and share transfers. Given that Securitize had already built its business within the existing regulatory framework, I would argue that this change is neutral at best. The SEC is broadly supportive of tokenization as a technology, but it likely won't allow tokenized securities to escape securities regulations. For example, the SEC approved Nasdaq's proposal to allow tokenized securities to trade on its exchange and is considering a similar proposal from NYSE. The SEC is also making it more practical to integrate blockchain-based records into existing securities infrastructure, which could expand Securitize’s addressable market. This potentially strengthens the case for Securitize's transfer-agent business and could eventually enable the company to become the official recordkeeping layer for securities. Incumbent transfer agents, like Computershare, have the same opportunity, though. Securitize Securitize provides regulated, blockchain-native infrastructure that enables financial assets to be issued, managed, and traded as digital tokens. The company is initially focused on treasuries, funds, and equities and has found early success with BUIDL (Blackrock treasury fund) and in private credit. Securitize now has a fairly comprehensive platform that works with both the traditional finance and digital asset ecosystems. Its vertically integrated stack includes: Tokenization Distribution Asset servicing Figure 4: Securitize's Platform (source: Securitize) Securitize has also developed infrastructure solutions that both power its business and can potentially be monetized through partners. For example, the DS Protocol provides issuers with tools for managing tokenized securities throughout the lifecycle and smart contract infrastructure for issuers, investors, and exchanges. This encompasses important areas like dividends, voting rights, and transfer and trading. Securitize also has the Vault Registrar, which standardizes the compliance layer for agentic finance using tokenized securities. It is a smart contract system that lets investors use tokenized securities in DeFi applications while maintaining the link between the token and its owner's identity. Rather than pooling assets from many investors for use cases like lending, the Vault Registrar uses a dedicated smart contract vault that is associated with an individual investor's identity. Figure 5: AI Vault Registrar (source: Securitize) Regulatory licenses are also an important part of the business. Securitize is a formally registered Transfer Agent with the SEC, a Broker-Dealer registered with both the SEC and FINRA, and holds an Alternative Trading System license which enables it to issue and trade security tokens. SEC-registered transfer agents are permitted to maintain and update the official ownership records of publicly traded securities. A broker-dealer can both facilitate securities transactions and buy/sell securities for its own account. Securitize received FINRA approvals for expanded broker-dealer capabilities in the second quarter of 2026. This included approval to custody tokenized securities within its broker-dealer and participate as an underwriter or selling-group member in IPOs and secondary securities offerings. Securitize also has a digital assets-focused fund administration business, which came through the acquisition of MG Stover's fund administration business in 2025. MG Stover was an experienced administrator of digital asset funds, providing services like fund accounting, investor reporting, subscriptions and redemptions, and operational compliance. At the time of the acquisition, the business was servicing 715 funds with 38 billion USD AUM. Fund administration provides Securitize with increased vertical integration, a more recurring source of revenue, and cross-selling opportunities. The business can be labor intensive, though, and so I would not assume that it has high margins. Securitize is largely positioning itself as the infrastructure that connects traditional securities markets to blockchain markets. As a result, partnerships with incumbent financial system players are important to the company's success. Securitize has partnered with the NYSE to help develop its digital trading platform, with Securitize acting as design partner/digital transfer agent and Securitize Markets providing broker-dealer connectivity. Securitize has also partnered with Computershare and Continental Stock Transfer, two major conventional transfer agents, to support issuer-sponsored tokenized shares. Computershare explicitly says its master securityholder file remains authoritative, while blockchain records form part of the system used to administer the tokenized holdings. A point of concern for Securitize's tokenization infrastructure business is the fact that the company has faced IP issues in recent months. Liquid Rarity Exchange has alleged that Securitize's platform infringes patents covering digital marketplaces for fractional ownership interests and is seeking damages and an injunction. tZERO has also sent Securitize a cease-and-desist letter alleging that DS Protocol and Vault Registrar infringe on tZERO patents covering self-enforcing compliance controls for tokenized securities. These cases introduce uncertainty around potential damages, injunctions, licensing costs, and product development. However, it has not been established that Securitize has infringed patents or that its products will be prohibited. Competitive Landscape Securitize faces competition from a range of market participants, including: Incumbent market infrastructure companies Direct tokenization and servicing competitors Crypto-native distribution and DeFi platforms These competitors have different advantages, and the intensity of competition varies considerably across the value chain. Competitors only need to control the customer relationship, regulatory function, or infrastructure layer where economic value accrues, though. Securitize has obtained licenses and approvals so that it can operate within existing regulatory frameworks, which is a time-consuming and difficult process. The company's vertical integration also makes its business more difficult for competitors to replicate. The nascent state of the business makes it difficult to ascertain whether there is any genuine competitive advantage at the moment. Relative to traditional fund managers, Securitize believes that it is differentiated by its technology. While Securitize's technology provides differentiation compared to legacy players, these organizations have significant relationships and distribution capabilities. The adoption of tokenized RWAs could undermine advantages related to scale and distribution, though. Despite this, I believe that the ability of legacy players to adopt tokenization technology has been underestimated. There are a number of tokenization and asset servicing competitors that are yet to really differentiate themselves. tZERO combines securities issuance technology with a broker-dealer, an alternative trading system, digital-asset custody and settlement, and transfer-agent services. It has historically been more focused on regulated secondary-market trading infrastructure, though. While tZERO's collaboration with ICE provides credibility, data suggests that there is very little activity on the company's ATS. Securitize has broader servicing and issuance capabilities, while tZERO potentially offers stronger secondary-market infrastructure. Superstate is also focused on placing regulated investment funds and company shares on public blockchains. It competes directly with Securitize in issuer-sponsored tokenization, transfer agency, and fund infrastructure. Superstate has less traction with players in the existing ecosystem, though. In comparison, Securitize is differentiated by its vertical integration, reducing the need for issuers to coordinate multiple service providers. INX's platform combines primary issuance of regulated security tokens, secondary trading of digital securities, and cryptocurrency trading. The company was recently acquired by Republic, adding to its private-market investment and fundraising business. This enables the Republic to supply the issuer and investor relationships that an isolated ATS often struggles to develop. Securitize again offers greater vertical integration, but Republic's relationships could make INX competitive, particularly in the private-market segment. There are also asset managers with in-house tokenization capabilities, although I tend to think that these are more of a niche threat. Franklin Templeton began developing its Benji tech stack in 2017 and launched an on-chain money market fund in 2021. Capabilities also include a digital transfer agency and investor servicing. In addition, Franklin Templeton makes its platform available to other financial institutions. WisdomTree offers similar services under the WisdomTree Onchain Brand and has around 1.2 billion USD AUM across 15 tokenized funds. JPMorgan has the Kinexys platform, which is already being used for tokenized money-market funds. Kinexys provides the infrastructure connecting the fund's existing service providers to Ethereum. Citi is building tokenized securities infrastructure and recently launched tokenized depositary receipts for private-company shares, with Citi acting as issuer and custodian. There are also companies offering third-party tokenization, like Backed and Ondo. This avoids most of the issues that Securitize is trying to address but does not provide direct ownership of the underlying asset. These companies may find success, but I don't really view them as a direct competitor to Securitize. Figure 6: RWA Tokenization Competitive Landscape (source: Securitize) Incumbent financial infrastructure companies at various stages of the industry value chain could also end up competing with Securitize, even though Securitize is collaborating with many of these companies at the moment. For example, DTCC, Computershare, State Street, BNY, Broadridge, exchanges, and custodians could incorporate blockchain into their existing infrastructure. Blockchains like Ethereum and Solana could also provide increasingly sophisticated tokenization primitives, reducing the value of Securitize's technology layer. The Depository Trust & Clearing Corporation operates the primary clearinghouse and securities depository for US financial markets. Its subsidiary, DTC, wants to extend the existing securities depository model onto blockchain networks. DTC has a tokenization service where eligible securities can be represented by a token on an approved blockchain, with DTC continuing to maintain the authoritative records linking the token and underlying security. The SEC has authorized a limited tokenization service for 3 years in late 2025, and DTC plans on launching the service in 2026. DTC has already processed actual production trades involving tokenized DTC-held securities. DTC is well positioned if tokenization is primarily a post-trade infrastructure problem. Computershare is one of the world's largest transfer agents and could also be an important player in the tokenization market. It has so far chosen to partner rather than trying to build the entire tech stack independently but could eventually choose to build or acquire the technology. Computershare's approach tokenizes the actual issuer-sponsored share, whereas DTC is tokenizing the entitlement to a security held within the existing depository system. The distinction matters, as one involves blockchain-native infrastructure, while the other is just a modernization of existing infrastructure. Nasdaq has a number of tokenization initiatives that aim to enable equity trading, tokenized settlement, issuer services, and collateral management. The company also has a partnership to modernize post-trade infrastructure. Nasdaq recently received regulatory approval for its tokenized-equity framework. This involved changing its exchange rules to enable the trading of tokenized assets. Eligible securities would be tokenized at settlement through the DTC's tokenization arrangements. Nasdaq's Equity Tokens initiative aims to enable participating companies to retain control over the representation of their shares by integrating blockchain records with their share registry. This program is expected to launch in the first half of 2027. Figure 7: Securitize's Ecosystem (source: Securitize) Financial Analysis Much of the current focus on Securitize's success relates to AUM. While AUM is a useful indicator of scale, it doesn’t directly translate to revenue in a simple manner. Securitize generates revenue through a combination of infrastructure fees, distribution fees, transaction fees, and asset servicing. As a result, transaction volumes and assets under administration are likely to be at least as important as AUM to value creation. Figure 8: Securitize Revenue Model (source: Securitize) Securitize generated 14.4 million USD revenue in the second quarter, a decline of roughly 6% YoY. AUM totaled 4.3 billion USD in Q2, while AUA was 24.3 billion USD, and aggregate transaction volume was 5.3 billion USD. There are now 663 active funds on Securitize Fund Services. While growth has been weak in recent quarters, this comes against a challenging macro backdrop. Crypto markets have been down significantly since the high in the middle of 2025, and in its current nascent state, Securitize's business appears to be dependent on crypto speculation. Securitize is now expecting 70-80 million USD in revenue in 2026, implying in excess of 20% revenue growth at the midpoint. Guidance requires a material growth acceleration in the second half of the year, though, which could be difficult for the company to meet. While 20% growth would be a solid result, it could be considered disappointing in light of the nascent state of the market and the size of the opportunity. Management also recently reduced full-year revenue guidance from 85 million USD. Figure 9: Securitize AUM (source: Securitize) Figure 10: Transaction Volume on Securitize's Platform (source: Securitize) Figure 11: Fund Services AUA (source: Securitize) Securitize's adjusted EBITDA loss was 5.5 million USD in the second quarter. The company has failed to exhibit any operating leverage in recent quarters, although this isn't surprising given the lack of growth. Revenue mix has also potentially been a headwind in recent quarters. I would not draw any conclusions from current financials, though, as they could change significantly as the business scales, dependent on competition and which parts of the business drive growth. Securitize had a little over 40 million USD in cash at the end of the second quarter, along with roughly 90 million USD in debt. The company's 1.3 billion USD market capitalization also means that equity raises are a viable means of extending its runway. Cash burn has been sitting at a little over 5 million USD a quarter, meaning that capital isn't an immediate concern. Conclusion Securitize currently has a roughly 1.3 billion USD market capitalization, meaning investors are paying around 23x sales for a company offering modest growth and a business with uncertain economics. The size of the tokenization opportunity is driving Securitize's valuation as much as anything else, and I believe that consensus revenue estimates are far too aggressive due to tokenization hype. While Securitize's decision to pursue a regulated approach to tokenization is more defensible and provides the most upside, it also exposes the company to the risk of incumbents embedding tokenization in their existing businesses, limiting Securitize's opportunity. As a result, I believe that Securitize's share price is still too high for the multiple layers of risk that it exposes investors to. That is not to say that Securitize won't provide strong returns, though, just that it is difficult to assess the probability of this based on currently available information. The company is more likely to succeed if blockchain-native issuance and ownership models gain traction, and investors should keep an eye out for evidence of this. I believe that Securitize’s most compelling opportunities are the regulated tokenization and servicing of private credit and alternative investment funds and issuer-sponsored securities. It could be difficult for Securitize to tokenize highly liquid public equities within existing market infrastructure, though. As a result, I tend to think that the opportunity will be far more modest than many expect, particularly given Securitize’s questionable ability to convert AUM into revenue. Figure 12: Securitize Market Capitalization (source: Seeking Alpha)

Data.title: US Treasury Yields Top 5% Ahead of Fed Decision as December Rate Hike Looms
Data.body: Key takeaways US 10-year Treasury yields return above 5% Fed expected to hold rates after September increase December hike expectations keep pressure on stock valuations US Treasury yields climbed back above 5% on Wednesday, October 28, as investors awaited the Federal Reserve's interest rate decision and weighed the possibility of another increase before year-end. The benchmark 10-year yield reached approximately 5.01%, according to Trading Economics , up from around 5.00% in the previous session. The move comes after yields briefly slipped below that threshold last week, when concerns about AI stock valuations encouraged demand for government bonds. The Fed is widely expected to leave its benchmark rate unchanged at 3.75%-4.00%, but the bond market suggests investors remain concerned about inflation and the longer-term cost of borrowing. Treasury Yields Return to 5% Despite Expectations of a Fed Pause The latest increase follows considerable volatility in October, when the 10-year Treasury yield reached approximately 5.35% before retreating. That earlier bond selloff reflected rising energy prices, persistent inflation and concerns about the US government's borrowing requirements. A return to 5% matters because Treasury yields influence mortgage rates, corporate financing costs and the discount rates investors use to value future earnings. Even companies delivering strong results face a more demanding environment when investors can earn relatively high returns on government debt. Coinpaper previously examined this tension between corporate earnings and elevated bond yields, particularly for technology companies commanding expensive valuations. Fed Rate Decision: Why December Matters More Than October The Federal Reserve increased interest rates by 25 basis points in September, bringing its benchmark range to 3.75%–4.00%. However, economists overwhelmingly expect policymakers to pause this month. A Reuters survey of 100 economists found that 94 anticipated unchanged rates in October, while all respondents expected another increase in December. Those expectations were examined in Coinpaper's earlier Fed outlook , although market probabilities can change as new data emerge. Inflation remains the central challenge. September's consumer inflation reached 3.7% annually, while elevated energy costs have complicated the central bank's efforts to restore price stability. The combination creates an uncomfortable trade-off: raising rates could restrain inflation but also make borrowing more expensive for households and businesses. What 5% Treasury Yields Mean for Stocks and Bitcoin Higher long-term yields can pressure stocks even when the Fed leaves its short-term benchmark unchanged. That relationship was evident during September's S&P 500 decline , when stronger economic data lifted borrowing-cost expectations and weighed on equities. Bond yields also affect technology companies financing expensive AI infrastructure, potentially making future earnings less valuable in today's terms. Cryptocurrencies face a similar macroeconomic test. Ethereum has already experienced a difficult October, with the latest ETH price outlook highlighting pressure from institutional outflows and uncertainty surrounding the Fed. Meanwhile, investors have previously turned toward government bonds when elevated yields made fixed-income investments more attractive, a dynamic reflected in PIMCO's Treasury assessment .

Data.title: Crypto.com Launches Regulated US Crypto Perpetuals With Up to 5x Leverage
Data.body: Crypto.com and OG.com have launched regulated cryptocurrency perpetual futures for eligible US traders, marking another step toward bringing a product long associated with offshore exchanges into the regulated American derivatives market. The new contracts allow traders to take long or short positions on digital assets without a fixed expiration date and offer leverage of up to 5x. According to the official announcement from Crypto.com , the products are being distributed through OG.com's network, including the Crypto.com App for retail users and the Crypto.com Exchange for institutional and advanced traders. The launch comes as US regulators continue clarifying how perpetual-style crypto derivatives can operate inside the existing futures framework. Crypto.com Brings Perpetual Futures to US Traders Crypto perpetual futures have become one of the most heavily traded instruments in digital asset markets. Unlike traditional futures, which settle or expire on a fixed date, perpetual contracts are designed to remain open indefinitely as long as traders continue to meet margin requirements. The new Crypto.com and OG.com offering gives eligible US traders access to this structure through regulated derivatives infrastructure. The contracts support leverage of up to 5x and include common risk-management tools such as take-profit and stop-loss orders. Crypto.com says the products trade continuously, allowing users to maintain exposure around the clock rather than being restricted to traditional market hours. The exchange recently registered as an Introducing Broker with the National Futures Association, enabling it to distribute the products to US customers through OG.com's infrastructure. ( The Block ) Why Perpetual Futures Matter for Crypto Traders Perpetual futures play a central role in global cryptocurrency trading because they combine continuous exposure with leverage and do not require traders to roll positions from one futures contract into another. That structure makes them particularly useful for short-term traders, market makers and investors looking to hedge spot exposure. A trader holding Bitcoin, for example, can open a short perpetual position to reduce downside exposure without selling the underlying BTC. At the same time, leverage allows traders to control positions larger than their posted margin. That can increase capital efficiency, but it also magnifies losses. A 5x leveraged position moves approximately five times as much relative to the trader's initial margin compared with the same unleveraged exposure. For that reason, the introduction of regulated US perpetuals is not simply a matter of adding another trading pair. It creates a domestic venue for a type of leveraged product that US traders previously often accessed through offshore platforms. The CFTC Has Been Opening the Door to Crypto Perpetuals The regulatory environment changed significantly earlier in 2026. In May, the Commodity Futures Trading Commission issued a policy statement concerning perpetual contracts , clarifying that perpetual products can be listed within the US futures framework subject to appropriate review. The CFTC also addressed the treatment of crypto perpetuals offered through regulated intermediaries. In a separate May 29 staff action , the regulator confirmed that certain digital commodity perpetuals could be treated as foreign futures under existing rules. That decision related to Coinbase Financial Markets and its planned access to perpetual products listed through Deribit. In June, the CFTC went further by granting no-action relief allowing designated contract markets to convert perpetual-style digital commodity futures into true perpetual futures . The regulatory direction has therefore shifted from uncertainty over whether perpetuals fit within US derivatives rules toward defining how they can be structured and offered under regulated conditions. Crypto.com Joins a Growing US Perpetuals Market Crypto.com is not the first major platform to move into this segment. Coinbase and Kraken have already introduced forms of perpetual exposure for US traders. Coinbase has pursued access through its regulated futures business and Deribit infrastructure, while Kraken launched US perpetuals following its acquisition of Bitnomial. That competition suggests perpetual futures could become a much more important part of the US crypto trading market over the next year. Until recently, US retail crypto derivatives were relatively limited compared with platforms serving international customers. Offshore exchanges have long offered perpetuals with high leverage, deep liquidity and dozens or even hundreds of trading pairs. US platforms have generally operated under tighter restrictions. The emergence of regulated perpetual products narrows that gap without recreating the extremely high leverage commonly seen offshore. Why the 5x Leverage Cap Matters Crypto.com and OG.com's maximum leverage of 5x is notable because it is much lower than the leverage historically offered by many international derivatives exchanges. Some offshore platforms have offered leverage of 50x, 100x or more on major crypto pairs. Those levels dramatically increase liquidation risk. At 100x leverage, even a roughly 1% move against a position can be enough to wipe out the trader's margin, depending on maintenance requirements and fees. A 5x cap still introduces meaningful leverage but gives positions substantially more room before forced liquidation. The lower leverage profile also fits more naturally within a regulated market structure focused on margin controls, customer protection and risk management. Perpetual Funding Still Shapes Trading Costs Although perpetual contracts do not expire, they generally rely on funding mechanisms to keep prices aligned with the underlying spot market. When perpetual prices trade above spot, long traders may pay funding to short traders. When the market trades below spot, that relationship can reverse. Funding rates therefore become an important cost for traders who keep positions open for extended periods. A perpetual contract can remain open indefinitely in theory, but maintaining the position may become expensive if funding repeatedly moves against the trader. This is one of the key differences between using perpetual futures for short-term speculation and using them as a longer-term hedge. Regulated Perpetuals Could Shift US Crypto Liquidity The broader significance of the launch may be its effect on where US crypto derivatives volume trades. Perpetual futures dominate derivatives activity on many global exchanges. If regulated US platforms can offer comparable instruments, some trading volume that historically moved offshore could migrate toward domestic venues. That could improve price discovery and liquidity on regulated exchanges. It could also give institutional traders more options for hedging cryptocurrency exposure without relying on products with fixed expiry dates. Crypto.com and OG.com are positioning their launch around exactly that combination of continuous exposure and regulated infrastructure. US Crypto Trading Is Becoming More Derivatives-Focused The Crypto.com launch arrives as derivatives activity continues to become a larger part of professional crypto trading. A recent Coinbase Institutional market positioning report showed rising turnover across spot, perpetual futures, term futures and options markets. The report found that options turnover reached its highest level since November 2025, while perpetual and futures activity also increased. That suggests traders are increasingly using derivatives not only for leverage but for hedging, volatility trading and portfolio positioning. The arrival of more regulated perpetual products in the US expands that toolkit. A Major Shift in the US Crypto Trading Landscape Crypto perpetual futures are moving from regulatory edge case toward mainstream US derivatives product. The launch by Crypto.com and OG.com illustrates how quickly that transition is progressing. Eligible US traders now have access to continuous crypto futures with leverage, stop-loss and take-profit functionality through regulated market infrastructure. The CFTC's actions earlier this year created a clearer framework for those products, while competition between Crypto.com, Coinbase, Kraken and other platforms is likely to push the market further. For traders, the appeal is straightforward: perpetual futures provide flexible long and short exposure without contract expiry. The risk is equally straightforward. Leverage increases both potential returns and potential losses, while funding and liquidation mechanics can make perpetual trading significantly more complex than buying crypto on the spot market. As regulated US platforms expand their derivatives offerings, understanding those mechanics will become increasingly important for anyone moving from spot trading into leveraged crypto markets. Data.title: Initia Exploit Drains $2.7M After MoveVM Bug Allows Unauthorized Token Minting
Data.body: Initia is working to patch a critical vulnerability after an attacker exploited its MoveVM implementation to create unbacked assets and bridge roughly $2.7 million out of the network. The modular blockchain halted both its Layer 1 and associated rollups on October 23 after detecting the security incident. Initia later said the attacker had abused a bug in MoveVM's script caching mechanism, allowing malicious code to bypass security checks and manipulate the state seen by the virtual machine. The incident affected wrapped and bridged assets rather than Initia's native INIT token, according to the project. Initia Halts L1 and Rollups After Security Incident Initia stopped its Layer 1 and rollup networks at 15:41 UTC on October 23 while developers, validators, exchanges and security specialists investigated the incident. Initial reports from blockchain researcher Spreek suggested that an attacker had found a way to mint assets without authorization and had already moved more than $2.6 million out of the ecosystem. Initia subsequently provided more detail and confirmed approximately $2.7 million had been bridged out before the network was halted. The decision to stop both the base network and its rollups prevented further exploitation while developers investigated the vulnerability. Unlike an exploit confined to an individual decentralized application, the issue affected infrastructure at the virtual-machine level, making the potential impact considerably broader. MoveVM Script Caching Bug Was the Root Cause Initia's investigation identified the vulnerability in its implementation of MoveVM on Cosmos SDK. According to the project's incident update, the attacker exploited a flaw in MoveVM script caching. The bug allowed malicious code to bypass checks that should have prevented unauthorized state manipulation. The attacker was then able to spoof MoveVM state and credit themselves with assets that were not properly backed. This is an important distinction from simply minting additional native INIT. Initia said the exploit did not increase the supply of INIT and did not allow the attacker to mint native INIT tokens. Instead, the manipulated state resulted in the attacker receiving unbacked representations of assets including WETH, iUSD-related assets and USDC. The incident therefore exposed a vulnerability in how the execution environment handled state rather than a flaw in the monetary policy of INIT itself. Attacker Bridges Roughly $2.7 Million Out Before validators halted the network, the attacker was able to move approximately $2.7 million in assets away from Initia. Initia said the outgoing funds included approximately 105 WETH, around 1.4 million AUSD0 and roughly 1.08 million USDC. The assets were moved through infrastructure including LayerZero, Noble and Circle's Cross-Chain Transfer Protocol. The funds were subsequently converted into approximately 1,135.52 ETH and moved to an Ethereum address identified by the project. The use of cross-chain infrastructure illustrates one of the challenges facing blockchain security teams after an exploit. Once improperly created assets can be moved to another network and exchanged for liquid assets such as ETH, containment becomes considerably more difficult. Stopping the compromised chain can prevent additional transactions locally, but it cannot automatically reverse assets that have already reached another blockchain. Native INIT Supply Was Not Affected One of Initia's key clarifications following the attack was that the native INIT token itself was not vulnerable to the minting method used by the attacker. Early descriptions of the incident referred broadly to unauthorized token minting, leading to concerns that the exploit could have compromised INIT's supply. The project later said that was not the case. The vulnerability allowed the attacker to manipulate MoveVM state in a way that credited unbacked versions of other assets without modifying the corresponding legitimate token supplies. Native INIT was not minted as part of the attack. This distinction matters because an exploit capable of arbitrarily increasing a blockchain's native token supply could create considerably wider economic consequences. The approximately $2.7 million loss remains significant, but the incident did not compromise INIT's underlying issuance mechanism based on the information released so far. Initia Prepares Security Patch Initia has since drafted a fix for the vulnerability. The project said the patch is being reviewed by security partners before the Layer 1 and rollups are restarted. Rather than immediately bringing the network back online after identifying the root cause, Initia is keeping operations halted while the fix undergoes security auditing. The team has said it will provide a concrete restart plan once those audits are complete. It is also working with security partners on recovery efforts involving the assets moved during the exploit. A full post-mortem is expected after the investigation and remediation work are completed. Why Virtual Machine Bugs Are Particularly Serious Smart contract exploits usually involve an error inside an individual application. A vulnerability in a blockchain's execution environment presents a different risk. Virtual machines are responsible for executing the code used by applications on a blockchain. If assumptions inside that environment can be bypassed, multiple applications or assets may potentially inherit the same weakness. In Initia's case, preliminary findings indicate that script caching allowed specially constructed code to avoid the expected security checks. That turned an implementation detail in the execution layer into a mechanism capable of producing economically valuable, unbacked assets. The incident demonstrates why blockchain security audits cannot stop at application-level smart contracts. Virtual machines, bridges, cross-chain messaging systems, caching mechanisms and state-transition logic all form part of the security boundary. Cross-Chain Infrastructure Can Amplify Exploits The attack also highlights the role bridges can play during security incidents. The attacker did not simply create unbacked assets and leave them inside Initia. Those assets were rapidly transferred through cross-chain systems and converted into assets on Ethereum before the network could be stopped. That sequence reduces the time available for validators and protocol developers to respond. It also means that security monitoring increasingly needs to operate across several networks simultaneously. An anomaly beginning on one blockchain may become an Ethereum, Solana or stablecoin issuer problem minutes later if the assets can move through interconnected bridge infrastructure. Initia Incident Adds to 2026's Blockchain Security Risks The Initia exploit is another reminder that increasingly interconnected blockchain architectures create new security assumptions alongside their benefits. Rollups, bridges and modular execution environments allow applications to move assets and data efficiently across networks, but every additional layer introduces code and infrastructure that must behave correctly. Initia's response limited the exploit by stopping the network, while the project says the vulnerability has now been identified and a patch is undergoing audit. The next important milestones will be completion of the security review, restoration of the affected assets' backing and the orderly restart of Initia's Layer 1 and rollups. Until then, the network remains a useful case study in how a low-level execution bug can quickly become a multi-million-dollar cross-chain security incident. Data.title: Bitcoin Bounces, but Fed and Inflation Data Loom
Data.body: From a very precarious position at $79,400, the Bitcoin bulls were able to stage a recovery and push the $BTC price back above $81K. The Fed is expected to hold rates steady at the FOMC meeting, but if Fed Chair Warsh is hawkish, and if PCE data comes in hot, this could derail further gains for Bitcoin. $BTC bounces back: Resistance already met? Source: TradingView The short-term 4-hour chart reveals that the descending channel is still holding the price within. The $BTC price got all the way down to the bottom of the channel and looked precarious for a while. However, the bottom trendline of the channel and the horizontal support held strong and a bounce eventually occurred. This may have had something to do with an AI trade that appears to be back on , as some of the top AI companies began strong recoveries. If the current rally can continue, the top of the descending channel could be reached, with a breakout a decent possibility. If, on the other hand, the current resistance level together with the 100 SMA prove too strong, the next dip could already be about to take place. Uptrend is still unbroken Source: TradingView If we look at the positives in the daily chart we can start with a strong rally that is currently in its second corrective phase, with the uptrend unbroken. The present pattern formation of a descending channel is a bullish one. Even though it is guiding the $BTC price downward, this kind of pattern would normally break to the upside. If the price does reach the top of the channel, the breakout becomes more likely. The Stochastic RSI indicator lines in this daily time frame are just rising from the bottom. On passing the 20.00 level they will start to signal upside price momentum. If we then take the negatives, the descending pattern is no longer a bull flag , given that the price has fallen more than 50% of the flag pole. Then there is the 50-day SMA, which the $BTC price has just rejected from. Could this rejection have been a confirmation of a breakdown from this important moving average? A rally is still on the cards Source: TradingView When we look at the macro picture of the weekly time frame all we are really doing is speculating on how far down the $BTC price is going to correct before it turns back up and continues the new bull market. Whether it has already turned, or whether it comes down to $75,600 or even $70K , is probably immaterial in the grand scheme of things. The more patient the ascent, the further it can probably go. The weekly Stochastic RSI indicators are now in bearish territory. Unless there is a big turn around this week (which is entirely possible with the economic data releases ) the upside price momentum should be falling off from now on. In the RSI at the bottom of the chart, the story is quite different. Having broken above a 2.5 year descending trendline, the indicator line is continuing to hold and bounce above this trend, signalling that a rally could certainly still be on the cards … as long as the economic data allows.
